rationale: BLOCKED, leaning YES. I read the complete held EO 12361 (47 FR 18313, April 27, 1982): sec. 1 delegates the President's reporting function under sec. 6 of the Multinational Force and Observers Participation Resolution (22 U.S.C. 3425) to the Secretary of State; sec. 2 requires consultation with OMB, Defense, ACDA, the National Security Adviser and other agencies. It has no sunset and no savings clause. History: an empty catalog note and a 1989 Codification row 'Codified at Chapter 22, p. 373', i.e. still in the 1989 codification (a 1989 snapshot, not current status). The U.S. Code lead prints the order text as a note to 22 U.S.C. 3425 with no ending statement, which supports a YES hypothesis, but no attributed slice of that note is held and it was checked only through 2026-10-09. A delegation tied to a statute that still exists is plausibly current, but ACDA (named in sec. 2) was abolished in 1999 and the successor-agency effect of that change is a scope question I cannot resolve from held sources.
